metric: Split of US advertising spend by money type (national_brand / local_retail / classified / direct_response), 1994-2001
definitional_axes: money_type x medium where a compiler publishes the cross-tab
task: source hunt only - no estimation, no bridging, no assembly
schema_notes: Schema is the one named in the invocation: era / sources_found / pools_sourceable / verdict / proxy_leads. Four keys added beyond it and flagged here: era_name, coverage_window, negative_findings, access_warnings, claim_id_convention.

Claim IDs use the project's e{era}-{field}-{NNN} form in a new field namespace 'src', starting at e5-src-001. Verified against claims.json that no e5-src-* ID already exists; highest existing e5 numbers are buyers-013 and scale-013.

Every figure in key_figures is a value READ from the named source, not an estimate. Grades follow the rigor_spec: A = official statistics or filings, B = credible named reporting. No grade-C figure appears in this file, because no number here was derived.

Conflicting credible sources are never averaged. Where two compilers disagree on the same object (Coen vs MAGNA direct mail; Coen vs RAB radio; Coen 2001-vintage vs Galbi-restated national/local) both are carried with the gap stated.

sources_found.name: The DMA Report: Economic Impact - U.S. Direct & Interactive Marketing Today (Direct Marketing Association, study conducted by The WEFA Group), as reproduced in the DMA Statistical Fact Book 2001, 23rd edition, pp. 295-299
sources_found.compiler: The WEFA Group (Wharton Econometric Forecasting Associates) for the Direct Marketing Association
sources_found.institutional_home: Direct Marketing Association, New York (DMA merged into the Association of National Advertisers in 2018; the DMA as an institution no longer exists)
sources_found.what_it_measures: US DIRECT MARKETING advertising expenditure, in current dollars, by medium (direct mail, telephone marketing, newspaper, magazine, television, radio, other-including-interactive), each further split consumer vs business-to-business AND by intended purpose of the offer (direct order / lead generation / traffic generation). Separately publishes, for the same media, total US advertising expenditure on DMA's own universe definition and the direct-marketing PERCENT of each medium.
sources_found.object_caveat: This is NOT Coen's measured-media universe. DMA's denominator for 2000 is $339.3B, against Coen's $247.5B, because DMA counts telephone marketing ($73.2B) and an 'other' category ($32.0B) as advertising media. Any use of DMA's totals against a Coen-based grand total requires an explicit scope reconciliation. The per-medium PERCENTAGES are the transferable part: DMA's per-medium denominators sit close to Coen's (magazines $17.3B vs Coen consumer magazines $12.370B + business papers $4.915B = $17.285B; radio $19.4B vs Coen $19.295B; newspapers $49.4B vs NAA $48.670B).
sources_found.how_built: Econometric model plus DMA member surveys; a forecast-and-backcast product, not a census. Published years are a mix of historical and projected: the 2001 edition presents 1995 and 1999 as history, 2000 as an estimate-for-the-completed-year, 2001 and 2005 as forecasts.
sources_found.gap_in_window: 1994 is not covered - the Economic Impact study series begins with 1995. 1996, 1997 and 1998 are not printed as levels; the table gives compound annual growth 1995-2000 by medium, which constrains but does not publish them.
sources_found.access: FREE as read. Full 2001 Statistical Fact Book PDF retrieved and parsed at http://courses.washington.edu/dmarket/2001Factbook.pdf (1.61 MB, 403pp, HTTP 200). WARNING: this is a copy of a copyrighted DMA publication hosted on a University of Washington course site, not a publisher-authorised open release; the underlying Economic Impact report itself was sold. Earlier editions (1996-2000), which would carry 1994 and 1996-1998, were NOT found free anywhere. archive.org holds only the 1989, 2007 and 2011 editions.
sources_found.independent_of_project_sources: YES for the direct-response estimates themselves - WEFA's model and DMA's surveys share no input with Coen/McCann, IAB/PwC or NAA. PARTIAL caveat: the same Fact Book reprints Coen's own national/local table (p.6) for context, so the volume is not wholly independent even though the DR series is.
sources_found.reputation_note: Widely cited in the trade press of the period (Chief Marketer / DIRECT, DM News) and treated as the industry's reference direct-marketing size. Criticised then and since for a broad 'direct marketing' definition that flatters the category, and for blending survey with model output without publishing the model.

sources_found.name: MAGNAGLOBAL media-supplier advertising revenue, Direct / National / Local typology, as reproduced in the Statistical Abstract of the United States
sources_found.compiler: MAGNA Global (IPG Mediabrands), reproduced by the US Census Bureau
sources_found.institutional_home: Interpublic Group; reproduction by US Census Bureau, Statistical Abstract of the United States
sources_found.what_it_measures: Advertising REVENUE reported by media suppliers (top-down, net of the advertiser-side production and agency layers), classified first into three money-type domains - Direct, National, Local - and then into eight core media within them, with Political and Olympic revenue held outside the three domains.
sources_found.object_caveat: MAGNA's three domains are close to but not identical with the project's four pools. (a) MAGNA 'Direct' = direct mail + direct online (paid search, lead generation, internet yellow pages) + directories ONLY; it excludes direct-response television, direct-response print and telemarketing, so it is far narrower than DMA's direct-marketing object. (b) MAGNA has NO classified category at any level: newspaper classified sits inside 'Local newspapers', and internet classifieds sit inside 'Local digital/online' per the table's own footnote 5. (c) MAGNA counts supplier revenue, Coen counts advertiser billings at list price; the 2000 totals are $177.5B vs $247.5B, a 28% scope gap.
sources_found.how_built: Top-down from advertising revenue reported by media owners. Introduced in 2009 to replace the McCann-Erickson (Coen) series, with a backcast to 1980 computed on the new methodology.
sources_found.gap_in_window: 1994-1999 are NOT free. MAGNA's backcast covers them, but the only public renderings found are the Statistical Abstract tables, which begin at 2000. The MAGNA methodology document (Magna Global [2015]) and Letang & Leszega [2017] 'U.S. Advertising Forecast' are not public.
sources_found.access: FREE for 2000: US Census Bureau PDFs, retrieved HTTP 200. Statistical Abstract 2012 (131st ed.) Table 1279 'Forecast Summary - Media Supplier Advertising Revenues: 2000 to 2010'; Statistical Abstract 2011 (130th ed.) Table 1278, same title, '2000 to 2009'. LICENSED for 1994-1999. The project's adspend.json already carries magna with access 'LICENSED'; this finding narrows that to 'licensed except 2000, 2003-2010, which the Statistical Abstract published free'.
sources_found.independent_of_project_sources: YES methodologically - a top-down supplier-revenue count against Coen's bottom-up advertiser-billings count, with different primary inputs. GOVERNANCE CAVEAT: MAGNA and McCann-Erickson are both Interpublic units, and MAGNA was built to replace Coen's series, so the two are institutionally related even though they are not methodologically derived from one another. Treat as independent for cross-check purposes, but say so.
sources_found.reputation_note: Silk & Berndt (NBER WP 28161) treat MG8 as the successor-of-record to the McCann series and reproduce its typology as Figure 2a. They describe the changeover as 'a fundamental departure ... with respect to scope and granularity', which is the reason the totals do not line up with Coen.

pools_sourceable.national_brand: NO SOURCE FOUND for 'national brand' as such - no compiler in this window publishes a national-BRAND pool. What exists is a published 'National' geography pool, from three compilers, all of which include direct-response money inside it: (1) Coen/McCann Total National, free, annual 1994-2001, but includes direct mail and national Yellow Pages, and is vintage-unstable by 2.4% at 2000 (e5-src-014); (2) MAGNA 'National', free for 2000 only via Statistical Abstract Table 1279 at $53,494M, licensed for 1994-1999, and on a supplier-revenue basis 28% below Coen's universe (e5-src-005); (3) the 1997 Economic Census, which gives an official national-and-regional vs local advertising receipts split for broadcasting alone, one year, grade A (e5-src-011). Medium-level national/local also exists from NAA for newspapers (annual, grade B) and RAB for radio (2 years free, grade B). TRIED AND FAILED: Ad Age 100 Leading National Advertisers back file; CMR/TNS annual national totals (licensed and now effectively lost - only a 1999 fragment survives, e5-src-013); TVB, CAB and OAAA historical national/local tables (no free archive found); MAGNA 1994-1999 (licensed). CONCLUSION: national_brand cannot be sourced; it can only be constructed as National minus the direct-response and classified money sitting inside it. It stays a derived residual and the derivation, not the pool, is what should be graded.
pools_sourceable.local_retail: NO SOURCE FOUND for 'local retail' as such - same structural problem, mirrored. A published 'Local' geography pool exists from Coen (free, annual, Total Local $95,808M in 2000), MAGNA (free for 2000 only, Local $90,933M), the 1997 Economic Census for broadcasting (Local net $16,473,717k, grade A), NAA for newspaper retail (annual, grade B) and RAB for local radio (1999-2000, grade B, and disagreeing with Coen by $0.38B on local radio in 2000). All of these include newspaper classified inside the local total, which is exactly the money the project needs to pull out. TRIED AND FAILED: Kelsey Group local-advertising market sizings (their published local-market work starts mid-2000s); Borrell Associates (founded 2001, series starts after the window); Yellow Pages Publishers Association national/local annual tables (association dissolved into the Local Search Association, no free historical file found). CONCLUSION: local_retail cannot be sourced; it can only be constructed as Local minus classified.
pools_sourceable.classified: PARTIALLY SOURCED - and this is the pool with the best evidence in era 5. (a) NEWSPAPER classified, which is the overwhelming majority of the pool: NAA 'Annual Newspaper Ad Expenditures', all eight years 1994-2001, free, grade B, already in the project (e5-src-008, 2000 peak $19,608M). Independently corroborable at grade A from audited SEC filings of the public newspaper groups - verified live for Knight Ridder, which reports classified separately for 1998, 1999 and 2000 (e5-src-009). Independently reproduced with academic documentation, at a different vintage, in HSUS Millennial Edition Table De523-526 (paywalled, values not read). (b) ONLINE classified: IAB/PwC breaks classifieds out as a format for FY2000 (7%) and FY2001 (16%) only; for FY1999 it is inside 'Others' and for 1996-1998 there is no format split at all (e5-src-010). So online classified is sourced for 2 of the 8 years and has NO source for 1994-1999. (c) NON-NEWSPAPER, NON-ONLINE classified - shoppers, free community papers, trade-press classified, penny-savers: NO SOURCE FOUND. Tried the Association of Free Community Papers, Editor & Publisher International Year Book, and the Economic Census. TRIED AND FAILED for an official series: the 1997 Economic Census Information Subject Series publishes NO source-of-receipts detail whatsoever for the publishing industries (NAICS 5111 carries a dash), and the 2002 Economic Census newspaper product lines split advertising space by print / internet / other media and general / specialized newspapers, with no national, retail or classified cut. No government statistical programme anywhere measures classified advertising as a category in this window. CONCLUSION: the pool's dominant component is well sourced and upgradeable from B to A; the pool as a whole is not exhaustively sourceable and the residual should be declared rather than absorbed.
pools_sourceable.direct_response: SOURCED FOR 1995-2001, WHICH IS NEW - and it overturns the project's standing position. The dataset notes currently record direct response as 'not published by any compiler'. That is wrong: TWO named compilers publish it, on two incompatible definitions that differ by more than 3x on the same object, and neither was in the project. (a) DMA / The WEFA Group, 'Economic Impact: U.S. Direct & Interactive Marketing Today', reproduced in full in the DMA Statistical Fact Book 2001 pp.295-299 - direct-marketing advertising expenditure by medium for 1995, 1999, 2000 and 2001, with 1996-1998 constrained by published CAGRs, plus a direct-marketing-percent-of-medium cross-tab (e5-src-001 to e5-src-004). This is the only published money-type-by-medium cross-tab found for era 5, and it explicitly quantifies the direct-response television ($21.9B in 2000), newspaper ($18.4B), magazine ($9.8B) and radio ($7.7B) that the project's era-5 notes say 'are not separable in the Coen series'. Free as read, with a hosting caveat. (b) MAGNA's 'Direct' domain - $31,108M in 2000 (direct mail + direct online + directories), free for 2000 via Statistical Abstract Table 1279, licensed for 1994-1999 (e5-src-005). THE TWO DISAGREE ENORMOUSLY AND MUST NOT BE AVERAGED: DMA's 2000 direct-marketing advertising expenditure is $191.6B on a $339.3B universe; MAGNA's Direct is $31.1B on a $177.5B universe; the project's current construction is $47.5B on a $247.5B universe. As shares of their own universes: 56.5%, 17.5%, 19.2%. The spread is definitional, not empirical - DMA counts telemarketing and all direct-response placements in general media, MAGNA counts only three supplier categories, and the project counts direct mail plus national Yellow Pages plus performance-priced internet. GAP: 1994 has no direct-response source at all; the WEFA study series begins with 1995. TRIED AND FAILED: earlier DMA Statistical Fact Books (1996-2000 editions) not found free - archive.org holds only 1989, 2007 and 2011; the underlying Economic Impact reports were sold and the DMA no longer exists; USPS Revenue Pieces and Weight and Household Diary Study were identified as an official direct-mail volume rail but not retrieved within this hunt.

verdict: NO SOURCE, ANYWHERE, PUBLISHES THE FOUR-WAY SPLIT FOR ERA 5. The closest published object is MAGNA Global's three-way Direct / National / Local typology, which has no classified category at all and whose 'Direct' is far narrower than direct response; it is free for the year 2000 only (Statistical Abstract Tables 1278 and 1279) and licensed for 1994-1999. So the four-pool split remains a construction. But the hunt materially changes what the construction stands on, in three ways. FIRST, direct_response is not unpublished - it is doubly published, by DMA/WEFA (1995-2001, by medium, free as read) and by MAGNA (2000, free), on definitions that disagree by more than 3x. The honest treatment is to widen the direct_response interval to span the definitional range and cite both, not to keep a single Coen-derived floor. SECOND, classified is the strongest-sourced pool in the era, not the weakest: NAA covers all eight years at grade B, audited SEC filings can lift the newspaper component to grade A, and only the online sliver (2 of 8 years) and the non-newspaper fringe (0 of 8 years) are genuinely missing. THIRD, national_brand and local_retail are the pools that cannot be sourced at all - no compiler has ever published a national-BRAND or local-RETAIL pool, only National and Local geographies that contain the other two money types inside them. These two must stay grade C with an explicit derivation, and their intervals should widen to carry two newly documented instabilities: Coen's own 2.4% vintage restatement of Total National for 2000 (e5-src-014), and the 2.44x-to-2.69x Coen-vs-MAGNA gap on direct mail (e5-src-007), which is the line being subtracted out of National to make national_brand. TWO POOLS SOURCEABLE IN PART (classified, direct_response), TWO POOLS NOT SOURCEABLE AT ALL (national_brand, local_retail). Every grade-C money-type claim in era 5 should therefore stay grade C for national_brand and local_retail, and should be regraded on its source for classified (B, upgradeable to A) and re-derived with a widened interval for direct_response.

negative_findings.result: None exists. Census does not collect it, BLS produces only price indexes (newspaper advertising space PPIs, no expenditure), IRS SOI carries a single undifferentiated advertising deduction.

negative_findings.result: Not broken out. FY1999 classifieds sits inside 'Others' at 11% of a $4.6B year and cannot be separated; 1996-1998 have no format split at all.

access_warnings: The DMA Statistical Fact Book 2001 PDF is a copyrighted DMA publication hosted on a University of Washington course site. It was read in full, and everything transcribed from it in this file is attributed to the DMA/WEFA study by page. It is not a publisher-authorised open release and the link may not persist. Nothing was paraphrased from a source that was not actually read.
HSUS Millennial Edition Table De523-526 is PAYWALLED. Its title, coverage, columns and contributor were read from the free contents page; NO VALUES were read and none appear here.

MAGNA 1994-1999 is LICENSED. The 2000 column used here is free only because the Census Bureau reproduced it. The project's existing magna series access note should be amended from a blanket 'LICENSED' to 'licensed except 2000 and 2003-2010, free via Statistical Abstract Tables 1278/1279'.

CMR / TNS Media Intelligence annual national totals are LICENSED and now effectively LOST - the successor no longer publishes the historical file and no archive of the annual releases was found. Only trade-press fragments survive.
SEC EDGAR returns HTTP 403 to the WebFetch tool. The Knight Ridder filing was retrieved with curl and a declared User-Agent, as the project's era-5 notes already record.

proxy_leads.lead: Bottom-up sum of audited newspaper-group 10-Ks to validate NAA classified
proxy_leads.why: The public groups report retail / general / classified in audited dollars. Summing Gannett, Knight Ridder, Tribune, New York Times Co., Times Mirror, Dow Jones, McClatchy, E.W. Scripps, Lee, Belo, Washington Post, Central Newspapers, Pulitzer, Journal Register and Media General for 1994-2001 gives a classified SHARE from primary records that is genuinely independent of NAA's survey. Knight Ridder alone puts classified at 42.5% of its 2000 ad revenue against NAA's 40.3% industry-wide.
proxy_leads.grade_if_built: A for the covered companies; the industry grossing-up is the C step
proxy_leads.effort: medium - 15 issuers x 8 years, but only 3 numbers per filing

proxy_leads.lead: DMA-percent-of-medium applied to Coen per-medium totals
proxy_leads.why: DMA's 2000 direct-marketing shares by medium (newspaper 37.3%, magazine 56.6%, television 39.6%, radio 39.9%) sit on denominators that are close to Coen's, so the shares transfer with a stated scope reconciliation. This is the route that would finally separate the direct-response TV and print the project currently says cannot be separated - and it would move a large sum out of national_brand.
proxy_leads.grade_if_built: C, with a method naming DMA's universe gap and the denominator reconciliation as its two adjustment steps
proxy_leads.independence: high for the shares, partial for the denominators
proxy_leads.caution: DMA's 'direct marketing' is a deliberately broad category built by an association with an interest in the number being large. The share for television in particular (39.6%) is far above any other contemporaneous characterisation of direct-response TV. Treat it as the upper bound of a range, not as the estimate.

proxy_leads.lead: MAGNA 2000 column as a second money-type rail
proxy_leads.why: A complete Direct/National/Local decomposition of one era-5 year, free, from a compiler methodologically independent of Coen. It cannot be stitched (different universe, no classified category, one year only) but it is the best available cross-check on whether the constructed shares are the right shape.
proxy_leads.independence: high methodologically, with an IPG common-parent caveat

proxy_leads.lead: USPS Revenue, Pieces and Weight reports and the Household Diary Study
proxy_leads.why: Standard Mail (A) volume and revenue are official annual statistics covering the whole window, and the Household Diary Study measures advertising mail received per household. Together they are an official rail underneath the single largest direct-response line, and would adjudicate between MAGNA's $18.25B and Coen's $44.59B for 2000 by separating postage from media value.
proxy_leads.grade_if_built: A for the postal quantities, C for the translation into advertising expenditure
proxy_leads.independence: high - identified but NOT retrieved in this hunt

proxy_leads.lead: Coen 2001-vintage tables as a vintage rail on national/local
proxy_leads.why: The DMA Fact Book preserves Coen's contemporaneous 1999 and 2000 national/local tables. Running the project's money-type construction on both vintages bounds how much of the national_brand figure is a curation artefact - 2.4% at the Total National line, 50% at the internet line.
proxy_leads.independence: none - same compiler, different vintage; this measures instability, not truth

proxy_leads.lead: 1997 Economic Census broadcasting national/local as an official anchor
proxy_leads.why: The only grade-A official national-vs-local advertising split in the window. One year, one medium group, but it independently tests whether Coen's national/local ratio for broadcast is roughly right, which underwrites the whole geography-based decomposition.
proxy_leads.grade_if_built: A for the census figure; C for any reconciliation against Coen's broadcast lines

proxy_leads.lead: Editor and Publisher International Year Book, 1995-2002 volumes
proxy_leads.why: Not chased in this hunt for want of a free copy. It carries newspaper ad revenue by category and is the lineage HSUS Table De523-526 documents. Would give an independent vintage of the newspaper classified series, and possibly the non-daily and weekly classified that NAA's daily-centred series under-covers.
proxy_leads.access: print / library; no free digitisation found
proxy_leads.independence: low to medium - shares the NAA lineage

cross_checks.test: MAGNA total digital 2000 against IAB/PwC internet 2000

a.detail: national digital/online 5,665 + local digital/online 1,843 + direct online 560

cross_checks.reading: MAGNA and IAB agree on the internet total to a quarter of one percent, which raises confidence that MAGNA's split of that total across Direct, National and Local is a real allocation rather than a residual.

cross_checks.test: MAGNA total supplier ad revenue 2000 against Coen total 2000
cross_checks.reading: FLAGGED, and expected. Supplier revenue against advertiser billings at list price. The flag is a definitional finding, not a data error, and it is the reason MAGNA must be a cross-check and never a stitch partner for Coen inside era 5.

cross_checks.test: MAGNA direct mail 2000 against Coen direct mail 2000
cross_checks.reading: FLAGGED, and the largest divergence found. The project's entire direct_response pool rests on the Coen figure. Two named compilers put the same medium in the same year 2.44x apart. Neither is wrong; the objects differ. The direct_response interval must span this.

cross_checks.test: DMA/WEFA direct mail 2000 against Coen direct mail 2000

a.source: DMA/WEFA via Statistical Fact Book 2001 p.296

cross_checks.reading: DMA and Coen agree on direct mail to nine million dollars, which almost certainly means DMA took Coen's direct-mail line rather than estimating it. This is a WARNING about independence: DMA's direct-mail line is NOT independent of the project's existing sources, even though its direct-response TV, newspaper, magazine and radio lines are.

cross_checks.test: MAGNA local newspapers 2000 against NAA newspaper print total 2000

a.detail: local newspapers only; MAGNA also carries national newspapers 2,165 separately, giving 48,671 combined

b.source: NAA annual newspaper ad expenditures, print total

cross_checks.reading: MAGNA local plus national newspapers = 48,671 against NAA's 48,670 - a one-million-dollar match. MAGNA is carrying the NAA newspaper total and splitting it 95.6 local / 4.4 national. So MAGNA's newspaper line is NOT independent of NAA either, and MAGNA's national/local newspaper split is a different partition of the same total than NAA's national/retail/classified. Both facts belong in the concordance.

cross_checks.test: RAB total US radio revenue 2000 against Coen total radio 2000
cross_checks.reading: Within tolerance. Two independent compilers, same medium, same year, 2.7% apart - a useful calibration of how much a national/local split wobbles between compilers even when the total nearly agrees. MAGNA's radio for 2000 (network and satellite 1,065 + local 18,819 = 19,884) is a third rendering, 0.3% from RAB.

cross_checks.test: Independent aggregate for the money-type split itself
cross_checks.result: NONE EXISTS. There is no tax-based, census-based or national-accounts aggregate anywhere that measures US advertising by money type in 1994-2001. IRS SOI carries a single undifferentiated advertising deduction; the Economic Census carries no classified cut and only a one-year broadcasting national/local cut; BEA's national accounts do not partition advertising by buyer type. This is stated here explicitly, per the operating principle, rather than left implied.
